![Image](https://allwebs.ru/images/2026/02/09/087238c7f7ac7094be594580c58f6813.jpeg)

Why do I get green areas instead of a blue hologram? Is it due to insufficient exposure? But if I add more energy, the hologram is no longer bright.

posts.author: holomaker
posts.content_md: Nice job for a first DCG . There’s a variable somewhere between the green and blue areas … shoot more you’ll figure it out (so many variables), are these DCG contact copies ?

posts.author: Manul
posts.content_md:
Thanks! Not copy, from real object reflection hologram. My test scene

it works like an achromate, according to the literature, this happens if you dry it in 100% isopropanol at once, but I dry it sequentially in three baths. On bright holograms, I always have a slight turbidity in 100% isopropanol, if this is not the case, the hologram is not bright. I don't like it. I'm sure you can get a clean image somehow. Maybe the thickness of the photographic material should be less? 3-5 microns? About 10 microns.

![Image](https://allwebs.ru/images/2026/02/09/abb9748b7893a426c4e7bdea325dd47b.jpeg)

![Image](https://allwebs.ru/images/2026/02/09/0a25a687fbd14842e643473c15bd1126.jpeg)

Other plate.

50 µJ/cm2 overexposure. Again, it's unclear why the blue at the bottom is correct; it might be the thickness after all.

![Image](https://allwebs.ru/images/2026/02/09/1515c3d244cdb5072531f30883269b04.jpeg)

Batsignal

posts.author: holomaker
posts.content_md: The magic of DCG is all the possible variants,in the end make a different effect. What method are you using to coat with?

posts.author: Manul
posts.content_md:
the table is leveled horizontally, the paste is heated and a measured amount of gelatin is added with uniform spreading

There's a hypothesis that blue is strongly absorbed by the dichromatic layer, and a normal grating is produced only on the surface. And in the depths, there's a nonlinear recording. This leads to wideband reproduction.

532 may be key

posts.author: holomaker
posts.content_md: Sounds as if you may have variances in coating thickness . Spin coat , vail coat or mold coating ?

posts.author: Manul
posts.content_md: Yes, there is a problem with uniformity. But I think the layer thickness is too thick for 457 nm. It needs to be 2-3 times thinner.

posts.author: holomaker
posts.content_md: I recommend you change over to mold coating as you can control thickness….
